newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cuts key lending rate to 48 percent. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia cuts key lending rate to 48 percent. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]

text.p: Russia's Central Bank is cutting its refinancing rate to 48 percent from 60 percent from December 2, chief spokesman Alexei Sitnin said on Friday.
Sitnin did not comment on the reasons for the move that was announced after it was approved by the board of directors.
Treasury bill yields have fallen steadily in recent weeks, and year-on-year inflation in October at 27.2 percent was at its lowest level since economic reforms began.
The cut takes the rate to its lowest level since April 1992. It was last cut on October 21, from 80 percent.

The Central Bank does not lend any money to banks at the refinancing rate. But many central bank penalties and banking and business contracts in the banking system are tied to the refinancing rate, which has an important signal effect.
The Central Bank also changed the rates on its Lombard lending facility for commercial banks.
Rates on seven-day Lombard loans rise to 24 from 20 percent, rates on 14-day loans fall to 36 from 40 percent and on 29-day loans to 48 from 50 percent.
(Corrects previous rates from 30, 50 and 60 percent, respectively, and makes clear seven-day rate rises as a result.)
The rouble, which is tightly controlled by the central bank, showed little reaction. It was quoted at 5,516.5 to the dollar on the interbank market in quiet mid-morning trading.
